<target>### **3.5 Dynamic-Priority Scheduling**

Priority-based scheduling can be made more flexible by allowing the operating system to automatically adjust threads’ priorities to reflect changing circumstances. The relevant circumstances, and the appropriate adjustments to make, depend what user goals the system is trying to achieve. In this section, I will present a couple different variations on the theme of dynamically adjusted priorities. First, for continuity with Section 3.4, Section 3.5.1 shows how priorities can be dynamically adjusted for periodic hard-realtime threads using a technique known as Earliest Deadline First scheduling. Then Section 3.5.2 explains decay usage scheduling, a dynamic adjustment policy commonly used in general-purpose computing environments.</target>
